title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: handle client cancel/disconnect and support reconnect/resume with server timeouts
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Improves streaming lifecycle: client cancel handling, graceful disconnects, reconnect/resume support, and configurable server-side idle timeouts. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: streaming endpoints are sensitive to client lifecycle events. We observed cases where client cancels or abrupt disconnects left server sessions or KV cache in inconsistent states, and lacked a way for long-running streams to reconnect and resume. This PR implements a deterministic streaming lifecycle control surface: explicit client cancel semantics, graceful disconnect handling with configurable server-side idle timeouts, and a reconnect/resume mechanism compatible with the OpenAI streaming adapter. Summary of changes: added resume tokens and session state tracking, changed session manager to track active streams with last-seen heartbeats, implemented a reconnect handler that validates resume tokens and reattaches KV cache state, added server-side idle timeout configuration to automatically garbage-collect inactive sessions, tightened race conditions on client cancel to ensure KV-cache cleanup and avoid duplicate completion events, updated openai_compat adapter to surface reconnect/resume fields and maintain streaming compatibility, added integration and e2e tests that simulate disconnect/reconnect and client cancel scenarios, and updated docs and migration notes. Checklist: 1) Implementation and unit tests added, 2) Integration tests for reconnect/resume and timeout-driven GC added, 3) OpenAI-compat adapter updated, 4) Docs and release notes updated, 5) Rollout plan added to description. Compatibility: this preserves the public REST/streaming API shape; reconnect/resume is opt-in via the streaming protocol and will not affect existing clients. Rollout: feature flagged behind runtime.feature.streaming_reconnect with gradual canary on Dedicated first, then hosted. Monitoring: new metrics for session_active, session_gc, reconnect_attempts, resume_success_rate. See release_notes for end-user impact. The description field is a single continuous string per repository artifact requirements.
